cues.en: Did you ever get angry on the Internet?

cues.en: It was all lowercase except for that one place where you needed to use the international phonetic alphabet because you don't know how to spell cash without it?
cues.zh: 全都是小写，除了那一处你不得不用国际音标，因为你不知道“淡定”这个词怎么拼？

cues.en: If so, you probably used uppercase or lowercase letters to get the job done. Uppercase signifies anger or yelling.
cues.zh: 如果是这样，你大概就是用大写或小写字母来达到目的的。大写代表愤怒或吼叫。

cues.en: Lowercase signifies that you don't care, lol.
cues.zh: 小写代表你不在乎，哈哈。

cues.en: Uppercase also has other uses.
cues.zh: 大写还有别的用途。

cues.en: For example, in German,
cues.zh: 比如在德语里，

cues.en: all nouns start with an uppercase letter for some reason.
cues.zh: 所有名词都莫名其妙地以大写字母开头。

cues.en: It's also traditional to start a person's name with an uppercase letter. This shows that you had the proper regard for their humanity and you took the time to press the caps lock key,
cues.zh: 传统上，人名也以大写字母开头。这表示你对他人的人格给予了应有的尊重，而且你特意花时间按下了大写锁定键，

cues.en: then press the first letter of their name,
cues.zh: 然后按下名字的首字母，

cues.en: then go back and press the caps lock key again to turn it off.
cues.zh: 再回去按一次大写锁定键把它关掉。

cues.en: So it's really useful that we have uppercase and lowercase.
cues.zh: 所以有大写和小写真的很有用。

cues.en: But what if I'm yelling and I want to show the proper regard for your humanity by capitalizing the first letter of your name? Then I want the letter to be uppercase,
cues.zh: 但如果我在吼叫，同时又想通过把你名字的首字母大写来表达对你人格的尊重呢？那我希望这个字母是大写，

cues.en: even more uppercase than before.
cues.zh: 比以前更大写。

cues.en: Similarly, I might want to be super casual and disregard your humanity with a lower case letter.
cues.zh: 同样地，我可能想表现得超级随意，用小写字母来表达对你人格的漠视。

cues.en: So that's what this video is about.
cues.zh: 所以这就是这个视频要讲的内容。

cues.zh: 但我对这些结果还是不太满意，所以我打算换个方法再试一次。

cues.en: Okay. There's two new ideas in this third try.
cues.zh: 好吧。这第三次尝试包含了两个新想法。

cues.en: First is, instead of representing this as a bunch of points and lines and curves, I'm gonna represent the input and output as a grid of pixels.
cues.zh: 首先，我不再用一堆点、线和曲线来表示，而是把输入和输出表示为像素网格。

cues.en: This is much more natural for a machine learning model anyway.
cues.zh: 反正这对机器学习模型来说要自然得多。

cues.en: But as you probably know,
cues.zh: 但正如你可能知道的，

cues.en: low resolution
cues.zh: 低分辨率

cues.en: fonts look pretty bad.
cues.zh: 字体看起来很糟糕。

cues.en: One standard solution to that is anti aliasing. So I can use instead of just black and white, I can use values in between black and white.
cues.zh: 一个标准的解决方法是抗锯齿。所以我不只是用黑和白，还可以用黑白之间的过渡色值。

cues.en: But there's actually a much better way to do this which I learned from Valve software of all places called signed distance fields. So this idea is pretty simple. You take your pixel grid and your shape that you want to rasterize.
cues.zh: 但还有一种更好的方法，我是从 Valve software 学到的，叫有符号距离场。这个想法很简单。拿你的像素网格和想要光栅化的形状。

cues.en: And for every pixel, you just compute how far it is from the shape. And if it's outside the shape, then it's... It will be negative. And if it's inside the shape, then the value will be positive. And in practice, you actually just use black to white with some gray value in between declared to be sort of zero. So instead of getting some pixelated garbage like this or even anti aliased pixelated garbage like this, you get some different looking pixelated garbage like this.
cues.zh: 对每个像素，计算它到形状的距离。如果在形状外，就是负的；如果在形状内，值就是正的。实践中，你其实用黑到白、中间某个灰色值来定为零。于是你不会得到这种像素化垃圾，甚至这种抗锯齿的像素化垃圾，而是得到另一种看起来不同的像素化垃圾。

cues.en: And the way you use this is you scale it up and then you apply a threshold
cues.zh: 用法是把它放大，然后应用一个阈值

cues.en: which is basically the value of zero on the edge and this gives you quite good looking images.
cues.zh: 这个阈值基本就是边缘上的零值，这样就能得到相当好看的图像。

cues.en: So I don't really care about scaling this up but I do care about the representation being really compact and yet containing a lot of information about what the font looks like.
cues.zh: 所以我不太关心放大，但我关心表示要非常紧凑，同时包含大量关于字体外观的信息。

cues.en: I'm gonna use 36 by 36 SDFs as input, and the same for the output except that I also have these 26 bonus outputs that predict the 26 letters as we discussed before.
cues.zh: 我会用 36 乘 36 的 SDF 作为输入，输出也一样，只是我还有 26 个额外输出，像之前讨论的那样预测 26 个字母。

cues.en: So that's idea number one.
cues.zh: 这就是第一个想法。

cues.en: Before we just trained one model, which makes letter shapes lowercase,
cues.zh: 之前我们只训练了一个模型，把字母形状变成小写，

cues.en: we trained it on examples from real fonts. It was fine at making uppercase letters lowercase, but it didn't really know what to do on lowercase letters. And it didn't really have any way to know because we only ever trained it on existing uppercase letters. Now the problem is I don't have any other examples except for maybe that one font I made, but that's not nearly enough. I would need like 10,000 of those. So what can we do?
cues.zh: 我们在真实字体的例子上训练它。它把大写字母变成小写做得还行，但遇到小写字母就不太知道该怎么办。它也没法知道，因为我们只用现有的大写字母训练过。现在问题是我没有其他例子，除了可能我做的那个字体，但那远远不够。我需要大约一万个这样的例子。那能怎么办？

cues.en: Idea two is that there is at least one property that we know, which is that lower casing is the opposite of upper casing.
cues.zh: 第二个思路是我们知道至少有一个属性，那就是转小写和大写是相反的。

cues.en: So the second idea is to train two models at the same time.
cues.zh: 所以第二个思路是同时训练两个模型。

cues.en: One that makes letters lower case, and another that makes them upper case.
cues.zh: 一个把字母变成小写，另一个把它们变成大写。

cues.en: So I still have all of the native training data, a pair of an uppercase and a lowercase letter from a font. And by swapping those around, those can be examples for making lowercase or for making uppercase.
cues.zh: 所以我仍然拥有所有原生的训练数据，也就是字体中大写和小写字母的配对。通过将它们对调，这些就可以作为转小写或转大写的训练样本。

cues.en: Now here's the trick. I can take a lowercase letter, say a lowercase a, and feed it to the make lowercase model, and it's gonna do something during training. It always makes some output. I don't know whether it's correct, but I do know that it's the lowercase of lowercase a according to this process,
cues.zh: 接下来是诀窍所在。我可以拿一个小写字母，比如一个小写 a，把它输入给转小写模型，它在训练期间就会进行处理。它总会产生某种输出。我不知道它对不对，但我确实知道根据这个过程，它就是小写 a 的小写形式，

cues.en: which means that if I flip that around, it's a training example for making uppercase.
cues.zh: 这就意味着如果我把它反过来，它就是一个转大写的训练样本。

cues.en: If I uppercase that thing, I should get a lowercase a. Symmetrically, can do the same thing with the make uppercase model by giving it an already capital letter. So the two models create training instances for each other,
cues.zh: 如果我把那个东西转成大写，我应该得到一个小写 a。对称地，我们也可以对转大写模型做同样的事情，只要给它输入一个已经是大写的字母。所以这两个模型可以互相为对方创造训练实例，

cues.en: which means that there's a feedback loop. And we ask the models to learn to be opposites of one another even if we don't have any idea a priori about what a lower or a case letter looks like. So training is grounded on all those real examples from fonts, but this feedback loop keeps it from getting too far off the rails or at least getting symmetrically off the rails if it does.
cues.zh: 这就意味着存在一个反馈循环。我们要求这两个模型学会彼此互为逆操作，即使我们事先完全不知道大小写字母长什么样。因此，训练是建立在字体中所有这些真实样本基础上的，但这个反馈循环能防止模型偏离轨道太远，或者即使偏离了也能保持对称。
